goal: Find and fix the bug that makes the last page of paginated search results come back empty.

turns.text: Users report that the last page of search results is sometimes empty even though the page count says it should have items. Pagination code: offset = page * page_size, and total_pages = total_items // page_size.

Two suspects there. If page is 1-indexed from the frontend, offset = page * page_size skips the first page entirely. And total_pages = total_items // page_size undercounts when there's a partial final page — 95 items at page size 10 gives 9 pages, dropping the last 5 items.
The frontend sends page starting at 1, yes. But wouldn't the off-by-one make every page wrong, not just the last one empty?

Good catch — a consistent off-by-one shifts every page, it doesn't empty the last one. So the floor-division undercount is the better fit for the symptom: the UI shows 9 pages, the user clicks page 9, offset lands at 90, and there are only 5 items left... which would still show items. Can you log total_items and the SQL offset for a failing request?
Logged it: total_items is 95, page_size 10, user requested page 10 from a stale UI, offset came out as 100. So the UI somewhere thinks there are 10 pages.

That's the real bug then: two different page-count calculations. The backend floors, but something in the frontend is doing ceil — Math.ceil(95/10) = 10 pages. The frontend renders 10 page buttons, the backend only has data through page 9 with its indexing, and page 10 at offset 100 is past the end.
Found it — the frontend does Math.ceil(total/pageSize) in the paginator component. Which one is actually correct, floor or ceil?

Ceil is correct: a partial final page is still a page. 95 items at size 10 is 10 pages, the last with 5 items. The backend should switch to ceiling division — in Python, (total_items + page_size - 1) // page_size, or math.ceil.
Quick tangent — why does everyone write (a + b - 1) // b instead of just calling math.ceil(a / b)?

The integer form avoids floating point entirely. math.ceil(a / b) goes through a float division, and for very large integers the float can't represent the quotient exactly, so ceil can return the wrong integer. (a + b - 1) // b stays in exact integer arithmetic.
Neat. Ok, back to the fix: I've changed the backend to ceiling division and offset to (page - 1) * page_size to match the 1-indexed frontend. Both page-count bugs and the indexing mismatch handled.

That covers it. Two edge cases to verify before you ship: total_items = 0 should give 0 pages, not 1, and total_items exactly divisible by page_size shouldn't produce a phantom empty page — ceiling division handles the second one correctly.
Wrote tests for both: zero items gives zero pages, 100 items at size 10 gives exactly 10 pages, and page 10 returns items 91 through 100. All green. Also added a test for the original 95-item repro.

Solid test coverage. One last thing worth checking: does anything else in the codebase compute page counts independently? The whole bug came from two components disagreeing — worth a grep for pageSize and page_size to make sure there's now a single source of truth.
Grep found one more in the CSV export feature doing floor division. Fixed it to use the same shared helper I just extracted. Three call sites, one implementation now.

That closes it out properly: root cause was divergent page-count math, fix was ceiling division in a single shared helper, and the regression tests pin the 95-item case, the exact-multiple case, and the empty case.
